questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the resolution rule in propositional logic?

options.text: To derive a contradiction from a set of clauses.
To convert a formula into CNF.
To simplify logical expressions.
To prove the satisfiability of a formula.

questions.explanation: The resolution rule is used to derive contradictions from a set of clauses, which helps in proving unsatisfiability and entailment.

distractorRationale.b: Converting a formula into CNF is a prerequisite for applying resolution, not the purpose of the rule itself.
distractorRationale.c: Simplification is not the primary goal of resolution; it aims to find contradictions.
distractorRationale.d: Resolution is used to prove unsatisfiability, not satisfiability.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a resolved clause from \( (A \lor B) \) and \( (\neg A \lor C) \)?

options.text: (B \lor C)
(A \lor C)
(B \lor \neg C)
(A \lor B \lor C)

questions.explanation: The resolution rule eliminates complementary literals, \( A \) and \( \neg A \), resulting in the clause \( (B \lor C) \).

distractorRationale.b: This option incorrectly retains the literal \( A \), which should be resolved.
distractorRationale.c: This option incorrectly introduces \( \neg C \), which is not part of the original clauses.
distractorRationale.d: This option includes all literals without resolving \( A \) and \( \neg A \).

questions.stem: Given the clauses \( C_1 = (P \lor Q) \) and \( C_2 = (\neg P \lor R) \), how many literals are in the resolved clause? Provide your answer as an integer.
questions.explanation: The resolved clause from \( C_1 \) and \( C_2 \) is \( (Q \lor R) \), which contains 2 literals: \( Q \) and \( R \).

questions.stem: Why do automated provers prefer clauses in CNF?

options.text: CNF simplifies the application of the resolution rule.
CNF is the only form that can represent all logical expressions.
CNF reduces the number of variables in a formula.
CNF is easier to read and understand.

questions.explanation: Automated provers use CNF because it allows for systematic application of the resolution rule, making the search for contradictions more efficient.

distractorRationale.b: While CNF can represent any logical expression, it is not the only form that can do so.
distractorRationale.c: CNF does not necessarily reduce the number of variables; it standardizes the form.
distractorRationale.d: Readability is not the primary reason for using CNF in automated provers.

questions.stem: Explain how resolution can be used to prove that a set of clauses is unsatisfiable.
markingGuide: Convert all given formulae into CNF.
Apply the resolution rule to pairs of clauses.
Continue resolving until either a contradiction (empty clause) is found or no further resolution is possible.
Conclude unsatisfiability if a contradiction is found.
questions.explanation: Resolution is used to derive contradictions from a set of clauses. By converting formulae into CNF and systematically applying the resolution rule, we can determine if a contradiction arises, indicating unsatisfiability.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the resolution method?

options.text: Resolution is complete for propositional logic.
Resolution can only be applied to quantified formulae.
Resolution is used to find satisfiability of clauses.
Resolution requires formulae in DNF.

questions.explanation: Resolution is a complete method for propositional logic, meaning it can derive any logical consequence from a set of clauses.

distractorRationale.b: Resolution is not limited to quantified formulae; it applies to propositional logic.
distractorRationale.c: Resolution is used to prove unsatisfiability, not satisfiability.
distractorRationale.d: Resolution requires formulae in CNF, not DNF.

questions.stem: Discuss the limitations of using resolution for automated reasoning in first-order logic.
markingGuide: Resolution is not complete for first-order logic without additional mechanisms like unification.
Handling infinite domains can be problematic.
Resolution requires conversion to CNF, which can be complex for first-order logic.
The search space can be large, leading to inefficiency.
questions.explanation: While resolution is complete for propositional logic, it faces challenges in first-order logic due to the need for unification, handling infinite domains, and the complexity of converting to CNF. These factors can lead to inefficiencies in automated reasoning.
